description.fun: Growlithe is loyal and fearless, barking at, biting and chasing off any threat to its Trainer or territory, even far bigger foes, and otherwise waiting motionless for orders. Its nose never forgets a scent and can even smell emotions. Its bones have been found in Stone Age ruins, and it's modelled on the shisa, the lion-dog guardian statues of Japan.
description.guide: A loyal, dog-like Fire Pokémon with orange fur and black stripes. It bravely defends its Trainer and territory and has an excellent sense of smell. It evolves into Arcanine with a Fire Stone, and its Hisuian form is a Fire and Rock type.
description.tagline: A loyal guard dog that never forgets a scent

description.fun: In ancient Hisui, volcanic activity in its coastal highlands gave Growlithe a fluffy grey mane of rock-like fur and a small, fragile rock horn. Hisuian Growlithe live in pairs and, having lived apart from people for so long, take a while to warm to them.

Arcanine can run 10,000 km in a single day, so gracefully it seems to fly, and anyone who hears its bark is said to grovel before it. In China it's revered as a Legendary Pokémon, and its official category is literally 'Legendary Pokémon', though it isn't one. Like Growlithe, it's based on the shisa, the lion-dog guardians of Japanese folklore.
description.guide: The evolution of Growlithe with a Fire Stone, a large, majestic dog-like Fire Pokémon admired for its beauty and speed. It is brave and loyal, and in some places it is revered as a Legendary Pokémon. Its Hisuian form is a Fire and Rock type with a rocky mane and horn.
description.tagline: The legendary dog that never made the Legendary list

names.ja: ヒスイ ウインディ

description.fun: Hisui's volcanic slopes gave Arcanine a grey mane of rock and a large horn. Bulky as it looks, it moves as nimbly as a dancer, and one Hisuian Arcanine, descended from a Pokémon blessed by Arceus, was worshipped as a noble Pokémon.
